text:
sana: Heads-up: quick UX review on the console nav regrouping. I made a tiny prototype of a compact sidebar where several items collapse under a single group row. Two gotchas surfaced for deep links and keyboard users. can we run through?

sana: Issue 1: deep links to item-level routes sometimes only expand the group but don't highlight the exact leaf node. The URL is correct, but the visual selection is the group.

ev an: saw that too. reproduction steps: paste /org/x/workspaces/alpha/dashboards/42/metrics into URL, nav expands group, highlights "Dashboards" (group) instead of "Revenue metrics" (child).

harper: Thought: matching algorithm is greedy prefix match which explains it. If nav keys are like /workspaces/:id/dashboards and children use /workspaces/:id/dashboards/:panelId, naive index might match the parent first.

sana: Suggested resolver order in my mock: fullPath exact -> pathParam-resolved map -> aliases (legacy redirects) -> longestPrefix fallback. This ensures exact leaf wins.

ev an: Agree. Also call out slug collisions where a child slug equals a group slug (e.g., "overview" used as group and also as item id). we should prefer exact id resolution.

noah: Accessibility: when we deep-link to a child, set focus to the child link and set aria-current="true" there. If expanding a group to reveal the child, announce group expansion and then move focus logically to the child. screen reader flow matters.

harper: Implementation detail: use history.replaceState to canonicalize to the resolved route after resolution, so shared links become stable. keep a short-lived query flag ?orig=<encoded> so we can show an optional banner explaining the route changed.

sana: Banner copy idea (inline, small): "We routed you to the closest matching page. Open the exact item" with a link. Should be dismissible and not appear on initial login redirect floods.

ev an: Maybe only show banner when resolvedRoute !== requestedRoute AND user has access to requestedRoute. otherwise silently canonicalize. Also rate-limit banner to once per session.

noah: keyboard support: hitting f to focus left nav should land on the highlighted item. If we canonicalize and change focus, ensure no focus jump traps in modals. add tests for Tab order and screen-reader announcement.

harper: question for eng: where do we store the alias/legacy map? central nav manifest or backend registry? I prefer manifest in source-controlled UI repo with a small API for runtime patches. keeps UX deterministic.

ev an: +1 to manifest. runtime can fetch and cache; we can ship fixes fast via a new manifest release. also add a small migration mapping for old ops anchors that used /# anchors.

sana: normalizer notes I pasted in figma: strip hash anchors, lower-case path segments, trim trailing slashes, sort query keys except session tokens. pseudocode:
```
normalize(path) {
  path = path.replace(/\/#.*$/, "");
  path = path.replace(/\/+$/, "");
  // lowercase segments and decode
  // stable-sort query keys except auth tokens
  return path;
}
```

noah: QA checklist (short): keyboard focus on deep-link, announce expanded group, aria-current on item, replaceState canonicalization, banner only when appropriate, test slug collisions, ensure back button preserves session state.

ev an: Action items: @evan will update nav-resolver PR to exact->params->aliases->prefix and add unit tests for collisions. @harper will prototype replaceState flow and demo. @noah will write a11y guidance + code snippets for aria attributes. @sana will upload compact and expanded mocks to the shared figma.

nav-bot: Preview link: https://console-preview.redwood/nav/compact-proto (note: ephemeral)

sana: Thanks team. FYI I'll also add a tiny animation so the highlighted item fades in after expansion to make focus movement less jarring. keeping it subtle. meet tomorrow 11am to validate with PMs.

ev an: I pushed a small test to the resolver branch. ping when demo is up.

noah: I'll paste the ARIA snippets here after I write them, might save eng a roundtrip.

sana: great :thumbsup:
